source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 17 aprilie — «Sfântul Ierarh Acachie, Episcopul Melitinei Armeniei»

feast.note: The Greek calendar keeps an Acacius the Confessor, bishop of Melitene, on 31 March, where the Romanian row on this folder holds 17 April. The same saint.gr page says that S. Eustratiades claims there was also an Acacius II, bishop of Melitene, and puts that one's feast on 18 April — so the site itself allows two bishops of this name and this see on two April days. The row records the day page that was read, and the identification with the man this folder already keeps rests on the see, the rank and the fifth-century anti-Nestorian work, which are the page's own; it is set down as a reading and not as a certainty, because a second folder for one man would be worse than an open question.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 31ης Μαρτίου — «Όσιος Ακάκιος ο Ομολογητής επίσκοπος Μελιτηνής»

attestations.note: The page heads him «(431 - ;)» and says «Ο Όσιος Ακάκιος έζησε τον πέμπτο αιώνα μ.Χ. (γεννήθηκε περί το 431 μ.Χ.)», born about 431 — and then has him distinguish himself when the heresy of Nestorius, patriarch of Constantinople, troubled the Church, write against Nestorius, and leave a surviving homily delivered at Ephesus. Those two statements cannot both stand: the Council of Ephesus met in 431. The year is the page's own and is recorded in `dates` with the contradiction named, and nothing is inferred to mend it. The page also credits him with virtue, learning and Orthodox zeal and calls him a most able speaker and teacher of the people. It prints no hymn; the one this folder carries is the Romanian troparion.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (20 September 2026).

hymns.text: Îndreptător credinţei şi chip blândeţelor, învăţător înfrânârii te-a arătat pe tine, turmei tale, adevărul lucrurilor. Pentru aceasta ai dobândit cu smerenia cele înalte şi cu sărăcia cele bogate; Părinte Ierarhe Acachie, roagă pe Hristos Dumnezeu să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfântului Ierarh Acachie, Episcopul Melitinei», Glasul 4

english.text: A rule of faith and a model of meekness, a teacher of abstinence — so has the truth of things shown you to your flock. Therefore you gained the heights by humility and riches by poverty. Father and hierarch Acacius, entreat Christ our God that our souls be saved.

birth.note: saint.gr: «Ο Όσιος Ακάκιος έζησε τον πέμπτο αιώνα μ.Χ. (γεννήθηκε περί το 431 μ.Χ.)» — the page's «περί», about, is why the display says about 431. The same page has him write against Nestorius and preach a surviving homily at Ephesus, where the council met in 431, which the year as printed cannot be reconciled with; the page's figure is recorded because it is the page's, and the contradiction is recorded with it rather than resolved. This folder held no `dates` before.
